title: AI regulations: Consultation paper in a month; safety, deepfakes among key focus areas, says Vaishnaw
key_facts: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw spoke on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 at the launch of the World Bank's 2026 World Development Report.
The government will put out a 'regulation-focused consultation paper which focuses on AI safety'; he asked the ministry to launch it within a month.
He linked it to deepfakes and said the harms 'are a nuisance which can cause huge problems'.
He said 'bulk of this regulation will have to be taken by the industry itself'.
Government will empanel some AI models or solutions so selected firms can bid in tenders from government departments.
The government has issued a request for GPUs: demand estimate 10,000, first tender 5,000.
The World Bank report says countries should avoid creating AI regulations that conflict with one another.
quote_evidence: The Union government will put out a “regulation-focused consultation paper which focuses on AI safety,” IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Thursday (October 8, 2026).
“We have to have the stakeholders onboarded because bulk of this regulation will have to be taken by the industry itself.”
“Our demand estimate is for 10,000 GPUs and the first tender that we are coming out is for 5000.”
why_it_matters_hint: India plans a public draft on AI safety and deepfakes within a month.
